write.desc: This topic proves the algebraic and order properties of the Riemann integral (linearity, monotonicity, additivity over intervals, the triangle inequality, integrability of compositions and products) and the mean value theorems for integrals; each is a theorem proved from Darboux sums and the Riemann criterion, so the points belong together as one section of working with sup, inf and partitions.

points.name: Integral of a sum
points.what: Prove that if f and g are integrable on [a,b] then f + g is integrable and its integral is the sum of the integrals, using U(f+g,P) <= U(f,P) + U(g,P), L(f+g,P) >= L(f,P) + L(g,P) and a common refinement.
outside: upper and lower Darboux sums and the upper and lower integrals
Riemann (epsilon) criterion for integrability
common refinement of two partitions and the refinement lemma for Darboux sums
supremum of a sum of functions is at most the sum of the suprema

points.name: Integral of a constant multiple
points.what: Prove that cf is integrable with integral c times the integral of f, handling c >= 0 directly and c < 0 by seeing that multiplying by a negative number swaps suprema and infima, and so swaps upper and lower sums.
outside: upper and lower Darboux sums and the upper and lower integrals
sup(cA) = c sup A for c >= 0 and sup(-A) = -inf A
Riemann (epsilon) criterion for integrability

points.name: Monotonicity and the bounds m(b-a) <= integral <= M(b-a)
points.what: Prove that f <= g on [a,b] implies the integral of f is at most the integral of g, by comparing lower sums partition by partition, and deduce that a function with m <= f <= M has integral between m(b-a) and M(b-a).
outside: upper and lower Darboux sums and the upper and lower integrals
definition of Riemann integrability as equality of upper and lower integrals

points.name: A continuous nonnegative function with zero integral is zero
points.what: Prove that if f is continuous, f >= 0 on [a,b] and its integral is 0, then f is identically 0, by finding a small interval where f stays above half of a positive value; and see by an example that continuity is needed.
outside: epsilon-delta definition of continuity at a point (a continuous function positive at a point stays positive nearby)
integrability of continuous functions on [a,b]

points.name: Additivity over intervals
points.what: Prove that for a < c < b, f is integrable on [a,b] if and only if it is integrable on [a,c] and on [c,b], and then the integral over [a,b] is the sum of the two, by adding c to partitions and splitting Darboux sums at c.
outside: Riemann (epsilon) criterion for integrability
refinement lemma: adding a point to a partition raises the lower sum and lowers the upper sum

points.name: Reversed limits and the oriented integral
points.what: Use the conventions that the integral from b to a is minus the integral from a to b and that the integral from a to a is 0, and check that additivity then holds for a, b, c in any order.

points.name: Integrability of |f| and the triangle inequality for integrals
points.what: Prove that |f| is integrable when f is, using ||f(x)| - |f(y)|| <= |f(x) - f(y)| to bound the oscillation on each subinterval, and deduce that the absolute value of the integral of f is at most the integral of |f|.
outside: Riemann (epsilon) criterion for integrability
reverse triangle inequality ||x| - |y|| <= |x - y|
sup minus inf of f on a set equals the sup of |f(x) - f(y)| over pairs of points

points.name: Composition with a continuous function
points.what: Prove that if f is integrable on [a,b] with values in [m,M] and phi is continuous on [m,M], then phi composed with f is integrable, by splitting the subintervals of a partition into good ones (small oscillation of f, controlled by uniform continuity of phi) and bad ones (small total length, controlled by the bound on phi); and see why continuity of the outer function is needed.
outside: Riemann (epsilon) criterion for integrability
uniform continuity of a continuous function on a closed bounded interval (Heine-Cantor theorem)
a continuous function on a closed bounded interval is bounded (extreme value theorem)

points.name: Integrability of f^2 and of products fg
points.what: Deduce from the composition theorem that f^2 is integrable when f is, and then that fg is integrable via fg = ((f+g)^2 - (f-g)^2)/4, noting that the integral of a product is in general not the product of the integrals.

points.name: Mean value theorem for integrals
points.what: Prove that if f is continuous on [a,b] then there is c in [a,b] with the integral of f equal to f(c)(b-a), by bounding the average value between the minimum and maximum of f and applying the intermediate value theorem.
outside: extreme value theorem for continuous functions on [a,b]
intermediate value theorem
integrability of continuous functions on [a,b]

points.name: Weighted mean value theorem for integrals
points.what: Prove that if f is continuous and g is integrable and nonnegative on [a,b], then there is c in [a,b] with the integral of fg equal to f(c) times the integral of g, handling the case where the integral of g is 0 separately.
outside: extreme value theorem for continuous functions on [a,b]
intermediate value theorem

where.title: Walter Rudin, Principles of Mathematical Analysis (3rd ed.)
where.detail: Chapter 6, Theorems 6.11 (composition with a continuous function), 6.12 (linearity, monotonicity, additivity) and 6.13 (products and |f|)

where.title: Kenneth A. Ross, Elementary Analysis: The Theory of Calculus (2nd ed.)
where.detail: Section 33, Properties of the Riemann Integral

where.title: Robert G. Bartle and Donald R. Sherbert, Introduction to Real Analysis (4th ed.)
where.detail: Sections 7.1 and 7.2 (properties of the integral, additivity theorem, products and compositions)

where.title: Michael Spivak, Calculus
where.detail: Chapter 13, Integrals (theorems on additivity, linearity and bounds, with problems on compositions and products)
